mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of 20-day windows where FEDFUNDS < 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate above 5.0% signals weakening labor market conditions, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy enters a slowdown phase.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by more than 1% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply-constrained economy (as indicated by a decline in industrial production), the S&P 500 tends to underperform over the next 20 trading days due to concerns about inflation and reduced corporate profits.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market (PAYEMS above 140,000) signals robust consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when PAYEMS > 140000.

mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market downturn (HOUST below 1000), the S&P 500 tends to underperform over the next 60 trading days due to reduced consumer confidence and spending.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when HOUST < 1000.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of housing starts (HOUST above 1000) signals strong consumer confidence and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when HOUST > 1000.
